title: 2023 Saudi Arabian GP: Alonso's 5 s penalty and the jack-contact ruling
text: 2023 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, car 14 (ALO). Lap 2: 5 second time penalty for an incorrect starting location. He served it at his pit stop; on lap 50 the stewards imposed a 10 second time penalty for serving the penalty incorrectly because the rear jack touched the car before five seconds had elapsed, dropping him from third to fourth. After a right-of-review request by Aston Martin the stewards withdrew the 10 second penalty, accepting that there was no agreed position that contact by a jack counted as working on the car, and his third place was restored. The sentence 'touching the car or driver by hand or tools or equipment will all constitute working' is absent from Article 54.4(c) in the 2023 Sporting Regulations Issue 4 (22 February 2023) and present from Issue 5 (25 April 2023).
source: OpenF1 race_control session_key=7779 (penalty messages); FIA 2023 Sporting Regulations Issues 4 and 5; race reports of the right-of-review decision
verified: penalty messages and laps from OpenF1; regulation wording from the FIA PDFs; reinstatement from press reports

title: 2023 Bahrain GP: Ocon's penalty served incorrectly
text: 2023 Bahrain Grand Prix, car 31 (OCO). Lap 15: 5 second time penalty for an inaccurate grid position. Lap 25: 10 second time penalty for serving that time penalty incorrectly. Lap 28: a further 5 second time penalty for speeding in the pit lane. A pending time penalty must be served as a stationary hold before any work on the car begins; failing to do so is itself penalised.

title: 2024 Austrian GP: Norris 5 s penalty for track limits
text: 2024 Austrian Grand Prix, car 4 (NOR). Lap 61: incident under investigation for track limits. Lap 64: 5 second time penalty for track limits. A 5 second time penalty is served as a stationary hold at the next pit stop or, if the driver does not stop again, added to his race time.
verified: penalty and laps from OpenF1 race_control

title: 2024 Mexico City GP: Verstappen's two 10 s penalties
text: 2024 Mexico City Grand Prix, car 1 (VER). Lap 13: 10 second time penalty for forcing another driver off the track. Lap 19: a second 10 second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage at turn 8. He made a single pit stop at the end of lap 26 (medium to hard) with a recorded pit time of 43.7 s, which included serving both penalties as stationary holds, and finished sixth.

title: 2019 Canadian GP: Vettel 5 s penalty for an unsafe rejoin
text: 2019 Canadian Grand Prix, car 5 (VET). On lap 48 Vettel ran wide through the turn 3-4 chicane, rejoined the track and forced car 44 (HAM), who was challenging for the lead, to take avoiding action. The stewards gave a 5 second time penalty for an unsafe rejoin. Vettel crossed the line first but was classified second because the five seconds were added to his race time.
source: Race reports (Autosport, PlanetF1) of the stewards' decision; outside OpenF1 coverage

title: 2024 Monaco GP: lap-1 red flag and the free tyre change
text: 2024 Monaco Grand Prix. The race was red-flagged on lap 1. Wheels and tyres may be changed while a race is suspended, and many teams switched compound during the suspension. Ten of the 16 cars with tyre data changed tyres under the red flag and then ran to the flag without another stop, having already used two different dry-weather specifications.
verified: red flag lap and stint counts from OpenF1

title: 2024 Sao Paulo GP: VSC stop versus red-flag tyre change
text: 2024 Sao Paulo Grand Prix (wet). Cars 4 (NOR) and 63 (RUS) pitted for fresh intermediates at the end of lap 28 under the VSC. Car 43 (COL) completed its last lap on lap 31 and the race was red-flagged on lap 32. Cars 1 (VER), 31 (OCO) and 10 (GAS), which had not stopped, fitted fresh intermediates during the suspension at no time cost. They finished first, second and third; Norris finished sixth. Intermediates were used, so the two dry-compound requirement did not apply.
source: OpenF1 stints, laps, race_control and position, session_key=9636

title: 2023 Singapore GP: Mercedes double-stack under the VSC
text: 2023 Singapore Grand Prix. Car 31 (OCO) completed its last lap on lap 43 and the Virtual Safety Car was deployed on lap 44. Mercedes pitted cars 44 (HAM) and 63 (RUS) at the end of lap 44 from hard to new medium tyres; cars may enter the pits under the VSC to change tyres. Measured against the non-stopping leader, Hamilton lost 19.4 s and Russell 16.7 s across their in- and out-laps, against about 30.5 s for a green-flag stop at this circuit. Car 55 (SAI) stayed out on hards and won from car 4 (NOR); Hamilton finished third.

title: 2024 British GP: intermediate-to-slick crossover timing
text: 2024 British Grand Prix (mixed conditions). The leading cars switched from mediums to intermediates at the end of laps 26-28 (Leclerc and several others had gambled on intermediates from lap 20). As the track dried, car 44 (HAM) pitted at the end of lap 38 for soft slicks and car 4 (NOR), who was leading, pitted one lap later at the end of lap 39, also for softs; Hamilton took the lead and won, Norris finished third. Car 1 (VER) took hard tyres and finished second. Because intermediates were used, the two dry-compound requirement no longer constrained the final slick choice.

title: 2021 Abu Dhabi GP: lapped cars before the final restart
text: 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. During the late safety car the race director allowed only the lapped cars between the leader (car 44, HAM) and second-placed car 33 (VER) to unlap themselves before the restart. For 2022 the FIA reworded the rule so that, once the message 'LAPPED CARS MAY NOW OVERTAKE' is shown, all lapped cars, not any, must pass the cars on the lead lap and the safety car.
source: Race reports and the 2022 Sporting Regulations change ('any' to 'all'); outside OpenF1 coverage

title: 2024: Magnussen race ban after reaching 12 penalty points
text: 2024 Italian Grand Prix, car 20 (MAG). A 10 second time penalty and two penalty points for a collision with car 10 (GAS) took Kevin Magnussen to 12 penalty points within twelve months. Under Article 4.2 of the 2024 Sporting Regulations a driver who accrues twelve penalty points has his licence suspended for the following Competition, so he missed the 2024 Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was replaced by Oliver Bearman.
source: FIA 2024 Sporting Regulations Issue 7 Article 4.2; race reports and Formula1.com
verified: Article 4.2 text from the FIA PDF; incident and ban from press reports

title: Pit entry closed: no tyre stop permitted
text: When the Race Director closes the pit entry for safety reasons (Article 34.15), drivers may only enter the pit lane for essential and entirely evident repairs. A driver who enters for any other reason, such as a tyre change, receives a penalty under Article 54.3(d), a ten second stop-and-go. A planned stop on a lap while the pit entry is closed must move to the first lap after it reopens.
source: Summary of Article 34.15 of the FIA 2025 Sporting Regulations, Issue 5
verified: paraphrase checked against the 2025 Issue 5 text

title: Pit-stop time loss: green flag versus SC/VSC
text: Pit-stop time loss is the time a car loses to the field by stopping. Measured field-relative across the in- and out-lap from OpenF1 data, green-flag stops cost about 30.5 s at the 2023 Singapore GP (three stops) and 24.2 s at the 2024 British GP (seven stops). Under a safety car or VSC the field is slowed while the pit lane speed is not, so a stop costs less: under the lap-44 VSC at Singapore 2023, Hamilton and Russell lost 19.4 s and 16.7 s to the non-stopping leader. The simulator assumes a neutralised stop costs 0.606 times the green-flag loss (13.2 s against 21.8 s on a generic circuit).
verified: measured from OpenF1 data in this repository

title: Wet races: the two dry-compound rule no longer applies
text: Article 30.5(m) requires each driver to use at least two different dry-weather tyre specifications in the race, unless the driver used intermediate or wet-weather tyres during the race. After an intermediate or wet stint a car may finish on a single dry compound. In a dry race, failing to use a second dry specification leads to disqualification, unless the race is suspended and cannot be restarted, in which case 30 seconds are added to the driver's elapsed time. The paragraph letter differs by year: 30.5(n) in the 2023 regulations, 30.5(m) in 2024 and 2025.
source: Summary of Article 30.5 of the FIA 2023 (Issue 6), 2024 (Issues 6 and 7) and 2025 (Issue 5) Sporting Regulations
verified: paraphrase checked against all four editions
